beats.say: Hi! A QR code is just a hidden link. You cannot tell where it leads by looking at it.
Scammers put their own QR stickers on parking meters, menus and posters.
When your phone reads the code, it shows the address. Before opening, check the domain: does it really belong to that organisation?
A QR code in an email can be a trap too. If the page asks for your password or card, stop.

scenes.prompt: Which QR codes are safe to open?

caption.text: Parking meter. You have a fine, scan and pay

cards.explain: Fines are not collected through stickers. Check fines only on the official portal or app.
The domain matches the cafe's name and the page only shows a menu. Nothing is requested.

caption.text: Your account verification expires. Scan to renew

cards.explain: An email with a QR code to verify your account is a classic trap. Open the portal yourself from a bookmark.

caption.text: DovletPortal certificate. Check it is genuine

cards.explain: The code leads to the issuing portal's own address and asks for no data.
Free internet never needs your card. An unknown domain plus a card request is a trap.
A shortened link hides the real address. Donate only on the charity's official website.

scenes.prompt: Find the suspicious parts of this email.

body.text: Our security system is being updated.
If you do not confirm within 24 hours, your account will be blocked.
Scan the QR code below with your phone.

spots.label: Foreign domain
spots.explain: The sender's domain is not ours: it is not rxagentlik.az.

spots.label: Urgency
spots.explain: The word urgent pushes you to act without thinking.

spots.label: Threat
spots.explain: The blocking threat is there to pressure you. Real support rarely writes like this.

spots.label: QR code
spots.explain: The QR code hides the link from the mail filter and moves you to a less protected phone.

question.prompt: There is a fine notice with a QR code on your windscreen. What do you do?

options.label: Scan it and pay right away
options.feedback: A fake page can steal your card details.

options.label: Check the fine myself on the official portal
options.feedback: Correct. If the fine is real, it will be there.

options.label: Call the number on the notice
options.feedback: The number may belong to the scammers too.

scenes.explain: Do not trust any contact on the notice. Open the official channel yourself.

nodes.text: At the cafe counter there is a QR sticker for quick payment. It is stuck on slightly crooked.

choices.label: Scan it and check the address first
choices.feedback: Good start. Checking the address matters.

choices.label: Scan it and pay right away
choices.feedback: The address was fake. Your card details went to scammers.

choices.label: Ask the cashier if the sticker is theirs
choices.feedback: Great idea. Asking is the simplest check.

nodes.text: Your phone shows the address: sahilpay-odenis.top. The cafe's name is nowhere.

choices.label: Pay anyway, I am in a hurry
choices.feedback: The rushed payment went to a scammer. The odd address was warning enough.

choices.label: Do not open it and tell the cashier

nodes.text: That is not our sticker! Please pay by card at the terminal.
nodes.speaker: Cashier
nodes.spoken: That is not our sticker! <short pause> Please pay by card at the terminal.

choices.label: Pay at the terminal
choices.feedback: Well done. You protected yourself and the next customers.

points: A QR code is a hidden link: check the address before opening.
Pay fines and bills only through official channels.
Never enter a password or card on a page opened by a QR code.
